title: Countries, nationalities and languages: je suis canadienne
summary: Say where you are from and where you live: en France, au Canada, aux États-Unis; je suis canadienne; je parle anglais.
focus: Countries with their gender and preposition, nationalities that agree, and languages
content:
## Countries have a gender

Every country is **feminine**, **masculine** or **plural**, and has its article:

| feminine | masculine | plural |
|---|---|---|
| **la France** | **le Canada** | **les États-Unis** |
| **la Belgique** | **le Japon** | **les Pays-Bas** |
| **la Suisse** | **le Sénégal** | **les Philippines** |
| **l'Italie** | **le Maroc** | |

Most countries ending in **-e** are feminine; the others are masculine. A few end in **-e** and are still masculine: **le Mexique**, **le Cambodge**, **le Mozambique**. Before a vowel, **le** and **la** become **l'**: **l'Allemagne** (f), **l'Iran** (m). Country names keep their capital letter.

## In, to and from a country

One little word means both *in* and *to*:

- **en** + a feminine country or one starting with a vowel: **en France**, **en Italie**, **en Iran**
- **au** (à + le) + a masculine country: **au Canada**, **au Japon**
- **aux** (à + les) + a plural country: **aux États-Unis**
- **à** + a city: **à Paris**, **à Montréal**, **à Dakar**

*From* is **venir de**, with the same pattern: **je viens de France**, **d'Italie** (before a vowel), **du Japon** (de + le), **des États-Unis** (de + les), **de Montréal**. To ask, say **Tu viens d'où ?** or **Vous venez d'où ?** (Where are you from?)

## Nationalities and languages

A nationality is an adjective: it agrees, takes **no capital** and, after **être**, no article (**elle est canadienne**).

| masculine | feminine |
|---|---|
| **français** | **française** |
| **canadien** | **canadienne** |
| **américain** | **américaine** |
| **belge** | **belge** |
| **suisse** | **suisse** |

Words already ending in **-e** stay the same. Only the noun for a person has a capital: **un Français**, **une Canadienne**.

Languages are **masculine** and lower-case, often the masculine nationality: **le français**, **l'anglais**. After **parler** they usually drop the article: **Je parle anglais.** Other verbs keep it: **J'étudie l'espagnol.**

## Vivre, habiter and the French-speaking world

| | vivre (to live) |
|---|---|
| je | **vis** |
| tu | **vis** |
| il / elle / on | **vit** |
| nous | **vivons** |
| vous | **vivez** |
| ils / elles | **vivent** |

**Habiter** says where your home is: **J'habite à Lyon.** **Vivre** says that too, and also *to live* in the wider sense: **Elle vit seule.** (She lives alone.)

French is spoken on every continent: **en Belgique**, **en Suisse**, **au Québec** (a province of Canada; the city is **à Québec**), **au Sénégal**, **au Maroc**. More than three hundred million people speak it.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Switzerland is a small country.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Montréal is a big city.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Is French a difficult language?

vocabulary.example_meaning: We live in France, in Lille.

vocabulary.example: Il travaille au Canada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He works in Canada.

vocabulary.example: Tu voyages aux États-Unis en juillet ?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Are you travelling to the United States in July?

vocabulary.example_meaning: Pierre is French and Julie is French.

vocabulary.example: Vous venez d'où ? — Je viens du Japon.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Where are you from? — I'm from Japan.

vocabulary.example: Nous vivons à Dakar, au Sénégal.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We live in Dakar, in Senegal.

quiz.prompt: Le Canada is masculine. Complete: Ma cousine habite ___ Canada.
quiz.explanation: A masculine country takes au (à + le): au Canada. En is for feminine countries, à for cities.

quiz.prompt: Ils passent les vacances ___ Italie. (They spend the holidays in Italy.)
quiz.explanation: L'Italie is feminine and starts with a vowel, so it takes en: en Italie.
hints: Feminine countries take a two-letter word.

quiz.prompt: Marie is from Toronto. Marie est ___.
quiz.explanation: The nationality agrees with Marie (-ien becomes -ienne) and, as an adjective, takes no capital: Marie est canadienne.

quiz.prompt: Le Japon is masculine. Je viens ___ Japon. (I come from Japan.)
quiz.explanation: Venir de + le Japon contracts: de + le = du. Je viens du Japon.

quiz.prompt: How do you write 'I speak English' in French?
quiz.explanation: Languages are masculine and lower-case, and after parler they usually take no article: Je parle anglais.

quiz.prompt: Nous ___ à Genève, en Suisse. (vivre: We live in Geneva.)
quiz.explanation: Vivre in the nous form is vivons: nous vivons à Genève.
hints: The stem is viv-, the ending -ons.

quiz.prompt: Le Mexique is masculine even though it ends in -e, so you say 'au Mexique'.
quiz.explanation: Most countries in -e are feminine, but le Mexique (like le Cambodge and le Mozambique) is masculine: au Mexique, du Mexique.
hints: It is one of the exceptions in the first section.

quiz.prompt: Les États-Unis is plural. Mes oncles travaillent ___ États-Unis.
quiz.explanation: A plural country takes aux (à + les): aux États-Unis.

quiz.prompt: 'Elle est Française' is correctly written with a capital F.
quiz.explanation: After être the nationality is an adjective, so it is lower-case: elle est française. Only the noun has a capital: une Française.
hints: Is française an adjective or a noun here?

listening.meaning: I come from France.
He lives in Portugal.
We speak English and French.

listening.text: Elle vit à Montréal, au Québec.
listening.meaning: She lives in Montréal, in Quebec.
listening.note: À for the city, au for the province.

listening.meaning: The students come from the United States.
Do you speak German or Italian?

listening.text: Au Sénégal, on parle français et wolof.
listening.meaning: In Senegal, people speak French and Wolof.

listening.text: Ma voisine est belge, mais elle vit en Suisse.
listening.meaning: My neighbour is Belgian, but she lives in Switzerland.
listening.note: Belge is the same in the masculine and the feminine.

guide.tip: Hear the country's article in your head first: la France → en France, le Japon → au Japon, les États-Unis → aux États-Unis.

concept.title: Hear the feminine
concept.markdown: The feminine ending is not only spelling: you can **hear** it. **Français** ends on an *s* you don't say, **française** on a *z* sound. **Canadien** ends in a nasal vowel, **canadienne** in a clear *n*. **Belge** and **suisse** sound the same for everyone.

conversations.title: At the language café
conversations.scenario: Awa, a student from Dakar, meets Lucas from Montréal at a language café in Lyon.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bonsoir ! Tu viens d'où ?
lines.meaning: Good evening! Where are you from?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Je viens du Canada, de Montréal. Et toi ?
lines.meaning: I'm from Canada, from Montréal. And you?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Moi, je suis sénégalaise. Je viens de Dakar.
lines.meaning: I'm Senegalese. I come from Dakar.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Et maintenant, tu vis à Lyon ?
lines.meaning: And now you live in Lyon?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Oui, j'étudie ici. Tu parles anglais ?
lines.meaning: Yes, I'm studying here. Do you speak English?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Oui, à Montréal, on parle français et anglais.
lines.meaning: Yes, in Montréal people speak French and English.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Moi, je parle français, anglais et wolof.
lines.meaning: I speak French, English and Wolof.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Le wolof ? C'est une langue du Sénégal ?
lines.meaning: Wolof? Is that a language from Senegal?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Oui ! Et mon frère vit aux États-Unis, à Boston.
lines.meaning: Yes! And my brother lives in the United States, in Boston.
lines.note: aux + a plural country, à + a city

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Super ! Ma sœur habite en Belgique, à Bruxelles.
lines.meaning: Great! My sister lives in Belgium, in Brussels.

bites.title: Every country has a gender
bites.rule: Feminine (la France), masculine (le Canada) or plural (les États-Unis). Most countries ending in -e are feminine; le Mexique is an exception.
bites.example: La Belgique est un petit pays.

bites.title: En, au, aux, à
bites.rule: En + feminine country or vowel, au + masculine, aux + plural, à + city. Venir de follows: de France, du Japon, des États-Unis.
bites.example_meaning: I live in Canada, in Toronto.

bites.title: Nationalities agree
bites.rule: No capital and no article after être: il est français, elle est française. Belge and suisse never change.
bites.example: Elle est suisse et il est américain.

bites.title: Parler + language
bites.rule: Languages are masculine and lower-case, and take no article after parler: je parle anglais.

sorts.title: En, au or aux?
sorts.why: Feminine countries (and vowels) take en, masculine ones au, plural ones aux.

sorts.title: Il est… or elle est…?
sorts.why: The feminine adds -e (-ien doubles the n: -ienne); a nationality already ending in -e fits both.

spots.why: Le Canada is masculine: au Canada.
Le Japon is masculine: de + le = du.
A plural country takes aux: aux États-Unis.
Paul is a man, so the adjective is masculine: français.
La France is feminine: de France, not du.

realm.content:
## Pays et peuples à Eldmark

Eldmark has its own lands: **la Valdorie** (f), **le Brennor** (m) and **les Îles d'Écume** (pl). So you travel **en Valdorie**, **au Brennor**, **aux Îles d'Écume**, and **à Highgate**. Nym **est valdorienne**; Borin **est brennois** and **vient du Brennor**. Each people has its language: **Nym parle elfique.**

vocabulary.example: La Valdorie est un pays de forêts.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Valdoria is a land of forests.

vocabulary.example: Highgate est la grande ville du royaume.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Highgate is the great city of the kingdom.

vocabulary.example: L'elfique est une langue très ancienne.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Elvish is a very old language.

vocabulary.example: Borin vient du Brennor.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Borin comes from Brennor.

vocabulary.example: Les nains vivent à Deepanvil.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The dwarves live in Deepanvil.

vocabulary.example: La mage Séla voyage en Valdorie.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mage Séla is travelling to Valdoria.

vocabulary.example: Il fait froid au Brennor.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's cold in Brennor.

vocabulary.example: Nym parle elfique et français.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nym speaks Elvish and French.

bites.title: Les pays d'Eldmark
bites.rule: Invented lands follow the same rules: en Valdorie (f), au Brennor (m), aux Îles d'Écume (pl), à Highgate (a city).
bites.example_meaning: The paladin is travelling to Brennor.

listening.meaning: Nym comes from Valdoria.

listening.text: Les nains du Brennor vivent sous la montagne.
listening.meaning: The dwarves of Brennor live under the mountain.
listening.note: New word: la montagne = the mountain.

listening.meaning: The mage Séla is Valdorian.
Do you speak Elvish, warrior?

listening.text: Le chasseur voyage aux Îles d'Écume.
listening.meaning: The hunter is travelling to the Foam Isles.

spots.why: Le Brennor is masculine: au Brennor.

sorts.title: À, en, au or aux in Eldmark?
sorts.why: Cities take à; feminine lands en, masculine lands au, plural lands aux.

quiz.prompt: Borin vient ___ Brennor, le pays des nains.
quiz.explanation: Le Brennor is masculine, so de + le = du: Borin vient du Brennor.

quiz.prompt: La mage Séla vient de Valdorie : elle est ___. (valdorien, feminine)
quiz.explanation: Like canadien → canadienne, valdorien doubles the n and adds -e: elle est valdorienne.

conversations.title: Where are you from, dwarf?
conversations.scenario: At the taverne du Dragon Vert, Nym the elf sits down next to Borin the dwarf.

lines.text: Je suis valdorienne. Je viens de Valdorie.
lines.meaning: I'm Valdorian. I come from Valdoria.

lines.text: La Valdorie, le pays des forêts ! Tu parles elfique ?
lines.meaning: Valdoria, the land of forests! Do you speak Elvish?

meadowbrook.content:
## Pays et langues à Meadowbrook

At **la fête des récoltes**, visitors come from everywhere. Rosa **vient du Portugal**: she **est portugaise**. Léo **vient de Belgique**; he **est belge** and **parle français et néerlandais**. Nora, the new farmer, **est canadienne**, and now she **vit à Meadowbrook**.

vocabulary.example: Rosa vient d'un pays très chaud.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa comes from a very hot country.

vocabulary.example: Nora aime la ferme, pas la ville.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora likes the farm, not the city.

vocabulary.example: Nora vient du Canada, elle adore le maïs.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora comes from Canada, she loves corn.

vocabulary.example: La nouvelle fermière est canadienne.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The new farmer is Canadian.

vocabulary.example: Les fraises viennent de la ferme de Nora.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The strawberries come from Nora's farm.

vocabulary.example: Léo vit près de la rivière.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Léo lives near the river.

vocabulary.example: Tout le village est à la fête des récoltes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The whole village is at the harvest festival.

vocabulary.example: Rosa est portugaise, de Porto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa is Portuguese, from Porto.

vocabulary.example: Mon voisin est suisse.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My neighbour is Swiss.

bites.title: À la fête des récoltes
bites.rule: Visitors say where they come from: de Belgique (f), du Portugal (m), des États-Unis (pl). Their nationality agrees: portugais, portugaise.
bites.example: Rosa vient du Portugal, elle est portugaise.
bites.example_meaning: Rosa comes from Portugal, she's Portuguese.

listening.meaning: Léo is Belgian, from Brussels.
Rosa speaks Portuguese and French.
The tourists come from the United States.
listening.note: New word: les touristes = the tourists.

listening.text: Nora vit à Meadowbrook avec ses poules.
listening.meaning: Nora lives in Meadowbrook with her hens.
Our neighbour comes from Switzerland.
listening.note: New word: la voisine = the neighbour.

spots.why: La Belgique is feminine: de Belgique.

sorts.title: Who is it at the festival?
sorts.why: The feminine adds -e (-ien becomes -ienne); belge and suisse fit everyone.

quiz.prompt: Le Portugal is masculine. Rosa de la graineterie vient ___ Portugal.
quiz.explanation: Venir de + le Portugal: de + le = du. Rosa vient du Portugal.

quiz.prompt: Nora vient du Canada. Elle vit ___ Meadowbrook maintenant.
quiz.explanation: Meadowbrook is a town, and towns take à: elle vit à Meadowbrook.

conversations.title: A new face at the festival
conversations.scenario: At the harvest festival, Rosa from the seed shop chats with Nora, the new farmer.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bonjour ! Tu es la nouvelle fermière ?
lines.meaning: Hello! Are you the new farmer?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Oui, je m'appelle Nora. Je viens du Canada.
lines.meaning: Yes, my name is Nora. I come from Canada.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ah, tu es canadienne ! Tu viens de Montréal ?
lines.meaning: Ah, you're Canadian! Are you from Montréal?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Non, de Québec. Et toi, tu es d'ici ?
lines.meaning: No, from Quebec City. And you, are you from here?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Non, je suis portugaise. Je vis ici avec ma fille.
lines.meaning: No, I'm Portuguese. I live here with my daughter.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Tu parles portugais avec elle ?
lines.meaning: Do you speak Portuguese with her?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Oui, à la maison. Et au marché, je parle français !
lines.meaning: Yes, at home. And at the market, I speak French!

rustwake.content:
## Pays et radios à Rustwake

Outside **le Dôme**, your **radio-montre** picks up voices from far away: **une radio du Canada**, **une station de Belgique**, **une voix des États-Unis**. Marta the trader **vient du Mexique**: she **est mexicaine** and **parle espagnol et français**. And you? **Vous vivez au village de ferraille** now.

vocabulary.example: Le désert de rouille est un pays sans eau.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The rust desert is a land without water.

vocabulary.example: La vieille ville est en ruines.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The old city is in ruins.

vocabulary.example: À la radio, on entend une langue inconnue.
vocabulary.example_meaning: On the radio, you hear an unknown language.

vocabulary.example: La radio-montre capte une station du Canada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The wrist radio picks up a station from Canada.

vocabulary.example: Le fouilleur vient de la station-service.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The scavenger is coming from the petrol station.

vocabulary.example: Le contremaître Ruiz vit dans le Dôme.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Foreman Ruiz lives in the Dome.

vocabulary.example: Ma radio-montre parle anglais !
vocabulary.example_meaning: My wrist radio is speaking English!

vocabulary.example: Marta est mexicaine, elle vend de l'eau.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta is Mexican, she sells water.

vocabulary.example: L'antenne capte une radio belge.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The antenna picks up a Belgian radio station.

bites.title: Voix à la radio
bites.rule: A station comes du Canada (m), de Belgique (f), des États-Unis (pl). The speaker is canadien, belge, américaine: no capital.
bites.example_meaning: It's a radio station from the United States.

listening.meaning: Marta comes from Mexico.

listening.text: La voix à la radio est canadienne.
listening.meaning: The voice on the radio is Canadian.
listening.note: New word: la voix = the voice.

listening.text: Le marchand parle espagnol et anglais.
listening.meaning: The trader speaks Spanish and English.

listening.text: Les fouilleurs vivent au village de ferraille.
listening.meaning: The scavengers live in the scrap village.
listening.note: New word: la ferraille = scrap metal.

listening.meaning: I'm listening to a station from Belgium.

builds.meaning: The radio comes from the United States.

spots.sentence: La radio capte une station de Canada.
spots.why: Le Canada is masculine: de + le = du.

sorts.title: Which station is it?
sorts.why: Masculine countries take du, feminine ones de, plural ones des.

quiz.prompt: Le Mexique is masculine. Marta, la marchande du village, vient ___ Mexique.
quiz.explanation: Le Mexique is one of the masculine countries in -e: de + le = du. Marta vient du Mexique.

quiz.prompt: On the wrist radio, a man and a woman from Brussels both say 'Je suis belge', and both are right.
quiz.explanation: Belge already ends in -e, so it is the same in the masculine and the feminine: il est belge, elle est belge.
